title: Zion Called to Awake
english: Book V, in six tomes. Tomos 1.
“Awake, awake, Zion; put on your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, the holy city. The uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you again” (Isaiah 52:1).

When you hear of Zion and Jerusalem here, do not think that only cities built of stone are meant. Rather, the word of the prophecy signifies the assembly of those called through faith, that is, the Church, drawn both from the ranks of the Jews and from the nations.

In saying “Awake,” and that quite often, he grants them the most abundant comfort. For just as, in the words of the all-wise Paul, “where sin increased, grace abounded all the more” (Romans 5:20), so where the bitterness of judgment is great, there the comfort matches the calamities, or rather far outweighs the gloom.

He has commanded her to put on her strength, and besides this her glory. Strength may fittingly be understood as the practical strength that works in action, by which each person's soul presses on with youthful spirit toward whatever must be done. And what else could glory be but the Lord of glory, who is Christ? To him the divine Psalmist speaks, at one time saying, “Awake, my glory” (Psalm 57:8), and at another, of everyone who believes in him, “You are the boast of their strength” (Psalm 89:17).

The all-wise Paul has made clear to us how we shall put on both the glory and the strength itself. For he said again, “Put on our Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires” (Romans 13:14); and besides this, “For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ” (Galatians 3:27).

Indeed, the prophet Isaiah too brings in the person of the Church as a woman adorned in many ways, saying, “Let my soul rejoice in the Lord, for he has clothed me with a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness” (Isaiah 61:10). So Christ is a robe most fitting for every saint, and a tunic of spiritual gladness, who gains for us strength and glory.

He calls the Church a holy city. For she was made holy, not through worship under the Law (for the Law made no one perfect; Hebrews 7:19), but by being conformed to Christ and becoming a partaker of his divine nature (2 Peter 1:4), that is, by sharing in the Holy Spirit, in whom we were also sealed for the day of redemption (Ephesians 4:30), when we washed away every stain and all …
